corrections.was: A Weighted sum adds several inputs, each multiplied by a weight that says how much it matters. Here each score has a closeness part and a health part. At one hundred fifty pixels and health zero point three, flee wins with zero point six six. Raise health to zero point eight and chase wins with zero point five one. For example, a boss could score calling for help as missing health times a big weight, plus nearby players times a small one.
corrections.now: A Weighted sum adds several inputs, each multiplied by a weight that says how much it matters. Here each score adds a closeness part and a second weighted part. At one hundred fifty pixels and health zero point three, flee wins with zero point six six. Raise health to zero point eight and chase wins with zero point five one. For example, a boss could score calling for help as missing health times a big weight, plus nearby players times a small one.
corrections.why: The slide's patrol formula is 0.6 x (1 - c) + 0.4 x 0.5, a closeness part plus a constant, so not every score has a health part.

corrections.was: Three strips of smooth noise, in this simulated run. A Seed is the number that fixes a random sequence. The values look random but are computed from the seed, which is why they are called pseudo-random. Seed forty-two, run twice, gives the same strip, with a largest difference of zero. Seed seven gives a different one. For example, the Walker level generator takes a seed, so seed seven builds the same level every time.
corrections.now: Three strips of smooth noise, in this simulated run. A Seed is the number that fixes a random sequence. The values look random but are computed from the seed, which is why they are called pseudo-random. Seed forty-two, run twice, gives the same strip, with a largest difference of zero. Seed seven gives a different one. For example, the Walker level generator takes a seed, so seed seven builds the same level every time on the same engine version.
corrections.why: Chapter 14 says a seed reproduces a level only on a pinned engine version, and Lab B's pass establishes determinism 'for a seed on this engine version', so an unqualified 'every time' overclaims.

corrections.was: Generate-and-test means making content at random, then checking each piece and throwing away whatever fails. Sixty seeds, one square each, and only twelve pass, twenty percent. With a policy of reject and re-roll, five playable levels took twenty seeds, so fifteen were thrown away. For example, a dungeon generator that keeps rolling new room layouts until the validator finds a path from the entrance to the exit is generate-and-test.
corrections.now: Generate-and-test means making content at random, then checking each piece and throwing away whatever fails. Sixty seeds, one square each, and only twelve pass, twenty percent. With a policy of reject and re-roll, five accepted levels took twenty seeds, so fifteen were thrown away. For example, a dungeon generator that keeps rolling new room layouts until the validator finds a path from the entrance to the exit is generate-and-test.
corrections.why: Chapter 14 (Lab B Verify) says a validator pass 'does not establish that an accepted level can be crossed', so calling validator-accepted levels 'playable' overclaims.
